stem: A 29-year-old woman, 3 months after delivery, spends about 3 hours a day washing her hands and repeatedly checking that the baby's crib is safe. She knows the thoughts are senseless but cannot stop them, and she is distressed by them. She is not breastfeeding. She has no hallucinations, no delusions and no periods of elevated mood.
oneliner: 29F + 3 mo postpartum + hours of washing and checking + knows it is senseless + no psychosis, no mania + not breastfeeding → which drug?
ask: Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy?

whyNot.A: Quick anxiety relief but **does not treat OCD**; dependence risk
whyNot.B: For psychosis; thoughts here are **ego-dystonic, not delusional**
whyNot.C: Mood stabilizer for **bipolar disorder**; no mania here

why: **Ego-dystonic washing and checking compulsions** = obsessive-compulsive disorder. **SSRIs** such as **sertraline** are first-line, usually with CBT.

drug.name: Sertraline
drug.how: Blocks presynaptic serotonin reuptake, raising synaptic serotonin
drug.use: Major depression, OCD, panic, PTSD, social anxiety, GAD
drug.watch: Sexual dysfunction, GI upset, insomnia, serotonin syndrome, hyponatremia (SIADH), discontinuation syndrome

stem: A 41-year-old man with HIV infection on stable antiretroviral therapy has had 6 months of burning pain and tingling in both feet that disturbs his sleep. Examination shows reduced pinprick and vibration sense in a stocking distribution and absent ankle reflexes. He has no history of substance use, and acetaminophen has not helped. A long-term oral drug for the pain is chosen.
oneliner: 41M + HIV on therapy + 6 mo burning, tingling feet + stocking sensory loss + acetaminophen failed → which drug?
ask: Which of the following is the most appropriate drug for his pain?

whyNot.A: Opioid; poor long-term choice for neuropathic pain, **dependence risk**
whyNot.C: Opioid; **same dependence concern** and no history of opioid use
whyNot.D: NSAID for **inflammatory** pain; weak for nerve pain
whyNot.E: NSAID for **inflammatory** pain; weak for nerve pain

why: **Burning feet + stocking sensory loss in HIV** = painful sensory neuropathy. **Tricyclics** such as **nortriptyline** (and gabapentinoids, SNRIs) relieve neuropathic pain.

drug.name: Nortriptyline
drug.how: Blocks norepinephrine and serotonin reuptake; also blocks muscarinic, H1 and alpha-1 receptors
drug.use: Depression, neuropathic pain, migraine prevention, enuresis
drug.watch: Anticholinergic effects, sedation, orthostasis, QT and QRS prolongation in overdose

stem: A 44-year-old man has had 3 months of waking at 3 to 4 AM and being unable to sleep again, loss of interest in his hobbies, poor energy and a 10-kg weight loss. He feels guilty and worthless. He has no hallucinations, no history of mania, and his physical examination and thyroid tests are normal. Drug therapy is started.
oneliner: 44M + 3 mo waking at 3-4 AM + anhedonia, low energy + 10 kg weight loss + normal exam and TSH + no mania → which drug?
ask: Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line drug?

whyNot.A: TCA: **anticholinergic effects and cardiotoxicity in overdose**; not first line
whyNot.B: Treats anxiety only; **does not treat depression** and causes dependence
whyNot.D: Partial 5-HT1A agonist for **generalized anxiety**, not depression

why: **Early-morning awakening + anhedonia + weight loss + low energy** = major depressive episode. **SSRIs** such as **paroxetine** are first-line.

drug.name: Paroxetine
drug.how: Blocks presynaptic serotonin reuptake, raising synaptic serotonin
drug.use: Major depression, OCD, panic, PTSD, social anxiety
drug.watch: Sexual dysfunction, weight gain, anticholinergic effects (most of the SSRIs), discontinuation syndrome, teratogenic risk

stem: A 46-year-old man who drinks heavily every day wants to stop. His last drink was 8 hours ago and he now has a tremor, anxiety and sweating. Pulse is 108/min and blood pressure is 152/92 mm Hg. He had a generalized seizure 2 years ago during an unsupervised attempt to quit. He is alert and oriented, with no hallucinations.
oneliner: 46M + daily heavy drinking, last drink 8 h ago + tremor, anxiety, tachycardia + prior withdrawal seizure → which drug?
ask: Which of the following is the most appropriate drug to give now?

whyNot.A: Lowers the **seizure threshold** and does not prevent seizures or delirium tremens
whyNot.C: Opioid antagonist to reduce **craving**, not to treat withdrawal
whyNot.E: Aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibitor for **aversion therapy**; would cause a reaction, not treat withdrawal

why: **Early alcohol withdrawal with a prior withdrawal seizure** needs a **benzodiazepine**. They **enhance GABA-A chloride channel opening** and prevent seizures and delirium tremens.

drug.name: Chlordiazepoxide
drug.how: Positive allosteric modulator of GABA-A; raises frequency of chloride channel opening
drug.watch: Respiratory depression with alcohol or opioids, accumulates in liver disease (use lorazepam or oxazepam), dependence

stem: A 9-year-old boy is in constant motion at school, rarely completes assignments and has had three emergency visits for injuries from reckless play. These behaviors have been present for 3 years in class and at home. He has had no treatment so far, and his examination is normal.
oneliner: 9M + constant motion + incomplete assignments + reckless injuries + 3 y at school and home + untreated → which drug?
ask: Which of the following is the most appropriate initial drug?

whyNot.B: Benzodiazepine: **sedation and disinhibition** in a child
whyNot.C: SSRI for **depression or anxiety**; not first line for ADHD
whyNot.D: MAO inhibitor with **diet and drug interaction risk**; no role here

why: **Hyperactivity + inattention across settings for years** = ADHD. **Methylphenidate** is the **first-line stimulant**.

drug.name: Methylphenidate
drug.watch: Appetite loss, insomnia, tachycardia, slowed growth, tics, abuse potential
